title: The annual Leonid Meteor Shower!
excerpt: WPDE covers news, sports, weather, and local events in and around the Grand Strand, Pee Dee, and the Border Belt.
content:
by Weather Authority Team

Mon, November 16, 2026 at 10:41 PM

Updated Mon, November 16, 2026 at 10:45 PM

The Leonids Meteor Shower kicks off late Tuesday night into early Wednesday morning

November brings the annual Leonid Meteor Shower - an opportunity to witness a shooting star!

This will be for late Tuesday night into Wednesday.

The Leonids Meteor Shower kicks off late Tuesday night into early Wednesday morning

The night sky show should have great conditions - mostly clear, but a bit on the chilly side, so dress to keep warm during those late-night hours.

Sky conditions look great! But dress for the chilly temperatures!

The meteor shower starts very late Tuesday night - around midnight, and goes through around 5am on Wednesday.

Look towards the eastern sky (constellation Leo) to hopefully see the shooting stars.

Best viewing time is between midnight and 5am Wednesday. Look to the eastern sky.

The expectation is for between 5-10 per hour near the city area, 10-15 across the suburbs and up to 20 per hour across inland/rural regions.

Happy viewing!

Dress warmly, and happy viewing!
